$comment: A TAG USED BEFORE A BLOCK'S OWN TAG OF THAT NAME NAMES THE OUTER ONE (C 6.2.1p7, C 6.7.2.3p5-p9; P69 round 1, lane cs, fold f26c -- the TAG form of D-C-A-NAME-USED-BEFORE-ITS-DECLARATION-BINDS-THE-LATER-ONE, its class-closure sweep). The scope tree binds a whole block's tags up front, and the tag lookup took the block's LATER `struct S` for a use written before it: a `sizeof` silently wrong, a member of the outer type refused. MEASURED by probe tg (the analyzer before this fold, pe64 and ELF x86_64, each RUN; the references on their legs). `struct S;` declares the block's own tag (C 6.7.2.3p7) and a use before its own scope's definition with nothing outside is that definition's tag -- both pinned here because the ordered lookup must not lose them. Every return before 42 names the first fact that failed; the release arm pins that the optimizer reads the same sizes.
